title: Digispice Technologies Ltd-$ - 517214 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: FY26 continuing-business PAT rose to about INR25 crore from INR6.5 crore, with gross margin up 13% to INR201 crore on 10.5% GTV growth.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a turnaround year, with continuing-business PAT of about INR25 crore against INR6.5 crore in FY25 and EBIT of about INR37 crore (2.4x). Gross margin rose to about INR201.2 crore from INR178 crore as higher-margin credit, insurance and banking products grew faster than AEPS cash withdrawal. Quarterly momentum was weaker in H2 because of state subsidy timing: management said Q4 gross margin was INR48.6 crore, INR3 crore below Q3. The company also launched UPI Cash Point in March 2026 and is waiting on RBI business correspondent banking-outlet guidelines and the Spice Money merger.

financial_highlights.change: vs about INR6.5 crore in FY25
vs INR39 crore loss in FY25
up 13% from about INR178 crore in FY25
up nearly 4% YoY after reclassification; management said revenue grew almost 12% before reclassification

segments.name: AEPS cash withdrawal (core)
segments.commentary: Spice Money GTV grew about 16% vs off-us AEPS industry growth of 9%; market share rose to 18.4% from 17.27%. Q4 share dipped on state subsidy cycles. Users rose to 11.3 crore from 10.6 crore, and subscription-pack users' share of GTV rose to 44% from 33%.

segments.name: AEPS Cash Deposit
segments.commentary: Management said it has grown consistently for 8 quarters as more banks went live; no FY26 value was given.

segments.name: UPI Cash Point
segments.commentary: Started formally in March 2026; run rate about INR100 crore GTV per month, with 30-35% market share claimed. Management expects it to reach about 50% of AEPS volume within 1-2 years.

segments.name: Collections (CMS and BBPS)
segments.commentary: Overall collections volume rose 7.4%; BBPS volume grew 12%, and BBPS rose to about 13% of collections GTV from about 9% in Q4 FY25. CMS clients (85) are being moved to BBPS agent EMI mode.

segments.name: Financial product distribution
segments.commentary: About 16.5 lakh accounts opened with Axis Bank and NSDL Payments Bank, with over INR305 crore float balance (about INR1,800 per account) and recurring float income above INR50 lakh per quarter. Loan distribution for 7 lenders reached INR539.6 crore in FY26 vs INR198.1 crore (2.7x). About 35,000 insurance policies sold.

segments.name: Credit (Adhikari loans, FLDG model)
segments.commentary: Disbursement rose to INR66.7 crore from INR20.5 crore (3.3x), running at about INR20 crore per quarter. Interest charged is 32-36%; management targets cutting it toward 24-26%. Credit is expected to turn EBITDA-positive in the current quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management expects profitability to grow about 20% YoY over the next 2-3 years, per the CFO.
Management expects Q4 gross margin run rate of INR50-52 crore per quarter going forward.
Credit business expected to turn EBITDA-positive in the current quarter; management sees credit growing 2x-3x annually.
Spice Money merger: NCLT first motion accepted; shareholder meeting next, with completion and listing targeted within FY27.
BC banking-outlet guidelines expected to be finalised by end-June 2026 and implemented around Q3 FY27.
Discontinued foreign-entity business expected to reach roughly zero expense in FY27.
capex_capacity: Agent network: about 16.6 lakh registered agents at March 2026 (up from about 1 million in FY22), across 2.57 lakh small towns and 6,400 blocks; 13.2 lakh agents are in Tier 4-6 towns.
Geography: about 84% of agents are in North, East and Central India; South and West hold about 16%.
Banking outlets: over 200 agent points have started converting to banking outlets with partner banks.
Roadmap includes own consumer app with UPI wallet, UPI ID and QR, plus a planned consumer CRM programme inside the agent app.
Spice Pay is in the build stage and is being in-sourced; management expects more Spice Pay products within two years.
demand_pricing: Competitive pricing pressure in cash collections (CMS), which management is addressing by strengthening supply-side and shifting clients to BBPS.
Subsidy cycles drove H1 above H2 revenue; management cited state-level subsidies and elections as seasonal drivers.
Management expects macro stress to hit discretionary spend, but says essential-payments volumes may hold and government financial-inclusion subsidies may help.
Management plans to expand into South India via UPI Cash Point and partnerships with microfinance and gold-loan players.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and FY28 outlook for top-line growth and EBITDA margins?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said profitability should grow about 20% YoY over the next 2-3 years; no explicit revenue or margin guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Plans to expand in South India?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said UPI Cash Point and financial product distribution open a South opportunity, with a goal of building a presence akin to the North within 2-3 years through partners.

qa_highlights.question: Adhikari loan growth, revenue and interest rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Repeat borrowers get larger tickets and longer tenure; the interest rate is 32-36%, with a path toward 24-26%. Growth could be 2x-3x a year, with FLDG protecting the company against losses.

qa_highlights.question: Why were H2 revenues weaker than H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman attributed it to subsidy timing, with more state subsidies in H1 than expected. CFO said part of the decline reflects reclassification and is not material.

qa_highlights.question: How does UPI Cash Point work, and what is the opportunity size?
qa_highlights.answer: Merchants sign up as BC agents and display a Spice Money QR; customers scan it to withdraw cash via any UPI app. Management sees it as a larger market than AEPS; it needs no separate regulatory licence, only a bank partnership under the BC framework.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 vs Q3 margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q4 gross margin was INR48.6 crore, INR3 crore lower, due to the subsidy cycle, lower Q4 revenue and one-time year-end adjustments; the run rate is about INR50-52 crore per quarter.

risks_watch: Subsidy-driven seasonality in AEPS: Q4 market share dipped and H2 revenue fell versus H1.
Pending RBI BC banking-outlet guidelines (consultation until June 2026), including the payment-bank branch-distance issue and the universal-bank rural-outlet obligation.
Credit portfolio quality under the FLDG model; the company bears first-loss exposure.
Macro slowdown could hit discretionary spend; management acknowledged impact is not ruled out.
Spice Money merger and listing timeline (targeted in FY27) and the exit from foreign-entity discontinued operations.
Whether UPI Cash Point reaches the targeted ~50% of AEPS volume within 1-2 years; one major UPI app still not live.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and profitability, with a turnaround message, but cautious on the near-term macro and regulatory timing. Management was direct about seasonality and one-time items, and deferred to guideline clarity on banking outlets.
key_quotes: So for the financial year 2026, from our continuing business, we have delivered a PAT of INR 25plus crores against about INR 6.5 crores in the previous year.
So effectively, from an AEPS -only platform, we are moving to UPI now.
So it's a onetime year-end closure, some onetime adjustments are there.
So it will be wrong to say that there will not be an impact.

UPI Cash Point product launched formally in March 2026, run rate about INR100 crore GTV/month
Spice Money merger (completion targeted within FY27) and BC banking-outlet guidelines (implementation around Q3 FY27)

growth.why: Management guides ~20% YoY profitability growth for FY27-FY29, backed partly by 16% GTV growth share gains, 3.3x credit disbursement, UPI Cash Point launch and 16.6 lakh agents; no quantified capex or new capacity and Q4 gross margin fell INR3cr QoQ to INR48.6cr.
